subject: Cross-border backup purge timeline & subprocessor safeguards
messages:
From: Sarah Willis <sarah.willis@medisynchealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Backup purge timeline for EU tenant + subprocessor checklist

Hi Grace,

We are finalizing our internal data governance review and need to confirm the timeline for backups/logs being purged for our EU tenant. Two asks: 1) Can Redwood provide the expected window (calendar dates) when backups are deleted after a retention expiry, and 2) for any retention-exception requests (legal/forensic holds) how does Redwood coordinate with subprocessors and what evidence/controls will MediSync receive?

We're also attaching our proposed DPA addendum (short edits) — can you confirm if these require changes to subprocessor contracts or operator playbooks on your side? We have a regulatory audit in Q3 and need the answers and any DocuSign-ready language by next Wednesday.

Thanks,
Sarah Willis
Head of Security & Compliance
MediSync Health
attachments: MediSync_DPA_addendum_v2.pdf
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Backup purge timeline for EU tenant + subprocessor checklist

Hi Sarah — thanks for the note and the addendum. Appreciate the timeline pressure. High level answers below, and I'm looping in Karthik and Priyom for the technical and subprocessor confirmation.

1) Expected purge window: for standard backups our policy is TTL + 7 days for snapshot tombstone and 30 days for long-term archival index removal. Practically, that means if a retention flag expires on 2027-06-01 we expect active snapshot purge to complete between 2027-06-02 and 2027-06-09 and archival index removal to finish by 2027-07-01. I will provide a more specific calendarized timeline for your tenant after Priyom confirms the snapshot cadence for your EU region.

2) Retention-exception / legal hold coordination: Redwood issues an internal hold ticket that is propagated to all affected subprocessor endpoints via our subproc API. We provide customers: (a) hold acknowledgement, (b) the list of subprocessors and their contact points, and (c) a confirmation once the hold is lifted or the purge completed. For audit purposes we can provide an evidence bundle (signed manifest + retention logs) tailored to scoped queries — Karthik, can we confirm the exact log artifacts and minimum retention for manifests?

Next steps: Priyom will confirm calendar dates for the EU tenant snapshot schedule; Karthik will list the evidence artifacts we can deliver and any limitations for on-disk logs; I'll review the DPA edits and suggest redlines if we need subprocessor contract changes. Can we aim to have this packaged (addendum + evidence spec + timelines) by Wed 2027-06-09?

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Manager, Trust & Safety Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 Jun 2027 14:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: RE: Backup purge timeline for EU tenant + subprocessor checklist

Grace / team — I pulled MediSync's tenant config and EU snapshot schedule. Quick summary:
- Daily incremental snapshots (00:30 UTC) retained for 45 days by default
- Weekly weekly-archive snapshots retained in cold storage for 365 days
- Tombstone propagation (metadata removal) executes in a staggered window starting at TTL expiry + 1 day, final check at TTL + 8 days

For this tenant, the standard timeline would therefore be:
- Active snapshot deletion window: TTL expiry + 1 to +8 days (calendarized in the spreadsheet).
- Cold archive finalization and index removal: TTL expiry + 30 days for index; object reclamation may take up to 90 days in worst-case cross-region deprovisioning.

If MediSync needs a hard carve-out (i.e., prevent any purge for a defined set of keys/paths) we can support a time-bounded exception by applying a scoped hold on the retention controller. That scoped hold requires a signed customer request and will trigger manual verification by SRE and a recorded playbook run.

I'm attaching a short workbook that maps your tenant's retention parameters to calendar dates and the change controls. If we issue a scoped hold, note the operational caveat: higher storage costs and a delayed archival lifecycle for affected objects.

Priyom
Senior Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 09:05:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Re: RE: Backup purge timeline for EU tenant + subprocessor checklist

FWIW on evidence artifacts: we can provide the following deliverables once the scoped objects are identified:
- Signed manifest of the hold + SRE ticks (PDF)
- Retention events log (immutable stream id + sequence) covering TTL expiry, hold creation, hold release (CSV export)
- Subprocessor propagation receipts (signed HTTP callbacks or email receipts depending on subproc)

Limitations / notes:
- On-disk forensic snapshots (raw disk images) are not provided by default; we can provide logical export of object keys and values for the requested time window.
- Some subprocessors (legacy backups vendor XferCloud) only provide asynchronous receipts; latency may be up to 72 hours for final confirmation. We should flag that in the DPA addendum.

Action for Kimberly / Laura: please confirm legal copy for the addendum that calls out XferCloud's asynchronous receipts and a mitigator clause (e.g., Redwood will escalate and provide alternate evidence if receipt latency > 72h).

Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer

Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 15:03:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Backup purge timeline for EU tenant + subprocessor checklist — proposed package

Sarah — thanks for the patience. Attached is a proposed package: (1) calendarized purge workbook for your tenant, (2) a DPA addendum redline that includes a clause about asynchronous subprocessor receipts and the escalation mitigator, and (3) a short evidence spec listing the artifacts we can deliver during an audit (signed manifest, retention events CSV, subproc receipts).

Key commitments in the package:
- We will provide a tenant-specific purge calendar (example: objects with TTL 2027-06-01 → snapshot deletion 2027-06-02..2027-06-09; index removal by 2027-07-01).
- Scoped holds available on customer request (requires signed request + SRE playbook run); we will record the hold and deliver a signed manifest.
- For subprocessors with async receipts (XferCloud) we'll include a mitigator clause and a 72-hour window for final confirmation; Redwood will provide alternate evidence and a root-cause write-up if receipt latency exceeds that window.

If this aligns, please confirm and indicate whether you want the addendum as a DocuSign package. If you need us to insert specific MediSync legal language, loop in your legal contact and we'll fast-track that.

Grace O'Connor
Manager, Trust & Safety Ops
Redwood Inference
